trust_decision.summary: An admin-writable setting (pypi_url) and its ENV['PYPI_URL'] fallback are stored with no validation at any write layer, then trusted verbatim by two independent models that hand the value to pip; the decision that the value is a plain http(s) URL has to be made where the value is consumed (a shared validator immediately before the pip invocation), not at the setter.

landing_point.why: It is the only shell interpolation of pypi_url in the tree (`output = `/openc3/bin/pipinstall #{pip_args}``, with pip_args built by string interpolation at :272/:274/:279/:281); an engineer given only 'OS command injection via the pypi_url setting' greps pypi_url and lands here first.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /openc3-api/plugins/install/:id -> PluginsController#install -> ProcessManager spawn of `openc3cli load` -> PluginModel.install_phase2 (same call reached by `openc3cli load` directly and by PluginModel#restore)

fix_sites.module_kind: model (second implementation: duplicates the pypi_url resolution and spawns pip itself)

fix_sites.entry_point: new OpenC3::PypiUrl utility called from both models (no public entry point of its own)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The packages route already passes an argv array into ProcessManager/ChildProcess (`spawn(["/openc3/bin/pipinstall"] + pip_args)`, operator.rb:122 `ChildProcess.build(*@process_definition)`), so it was never shell-injectable and 'needs no change' - yet the published fix added PypiUrl.validate there too.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Air-gapped/private index support: pypi_url is legitimately an http (not https) mirror with a host:port and a path, passed unchanged to pip and its host fed to --trusted-host when PIP_ENABLE_TRUSTED_HOST is set, so a validator restricted to https/pypi.org or one that normalises/strips the URL breaks private mirrors (the fix's own spec pins 'allows a host with a port'); the sink must also stay non-fatal, so raising instead of falling back to DEFAULT would abort plugin install when pip fails.

O6_input_shapes: pypi_url read from the Redis setting via get_setting (then '/simple' appended)
pypi_url from the ENV['PYPI_URL'] fallback (then '/simple' appended)
valid http:// and https:// URLs, including a host with a port
invalid strings - shell metacharacters, non-http(s) scheme, missing host, empty string, non-URL text - replaced by DEFAULT with a logged error
both plugin dependency layouts: pyproject.toml (gem directory as last arg) vs requirements.txt (-r path)
PIP_ENABLE_TRUSTED_HOST set (extra --trusted-host argv pair) vs unset

O7_producer.where: openc3/lib/openc3/utilities/local_mode.rb:470-490 (LocalMode.sync_settings reads <scope>/settings/*.json and writes them into Redis; save_setting writes them back) and openc3/lib/openc3/models/scope_model.rb:404-405 (seeds pypi_url from ENV['PYPI_URL'])

O8b_injection_room.sibling: rubygems_url, resolved from the same setting store in exactly the same way, handed to Gem.sources
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same air-gapped mirror feature written by the same authors in the same idiom; a maintainer adding a gem-side install that goes through a command line (or build_args) would repeat the pypi_url mistake verbatim.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the shell helper re-expands the caller's argv unquoted (`uv pip compile ${OPTS} ...` / `uv pip install ... ${OPTS} -r "$TMPFILE"`) on its retry path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A second, non-Ruby implementation of the same argument plumbing; a maintainer adding another placeholder there (e.g. an extra index) would reopen a shell word-split boundary in a place the Ruby validator does not reach.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: pipuninstall spawned with a package name derived from params[:id]
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The mirror-image sink next to the pip install sink; a maintainer writing a shell-string variant of uninstall (instead of the argv array used today) would be a realistic sibling copy.
